name: Santa Fe
blurb: Adobe galleries, Canyon Road, world-class Southwestern food, and the single biggest Native art market on the planet every August. Old-money art-collector scene, Ten Thousand Waves spa, Inn of the Five Graces.

name: Austin
blurb: Live-music capital energy, food trailers, Barton Springs, and 6th Street on Halloween weekend. Westlake Hills & Lake Austin carry tech/finance money, Barton Creek Resort, and the Miraval wellness retreat.

name: Denver
blurb: Breweries, RiNo street art, Red Rocks shows, and a genuinely great museum and food scene at mile-high altitude. Centennial Airport is Denver's busiest GA field — ten minutes from Cherry Hills Village and close to Cherry Creek North.

name: Kansas City
blurb: World-class BBQ, the Nelson-Atkins Museum, jazz history in the 18th & Vine district, and an underrated nightlife scene.

name: Dallas
blurb: Deep Ellum nightlife, one of the largest arts districts in the country, and the Cotton Bowl hosting the biggest rivalry game in college football.

airports.name: Fort Worth Alliance
airports.notes: serves the DFW metro

name: Fayetteville
blurb: College-town energy on Dickson Street, plus the doorstep to Bentonville's art scene and Eureka Springs' Ozark charm.

name: St. Louis
blurb: Free-admission Saint Louis Art Museum, the wild City Museum, Forest Park, and a classic Midwest food-and-beer culture.

name: Fort Worth
blurb: Cowtown culture at the Stockyards, plus a genuinely elite museum cluster (Kimbell, Modern Art Museum) minutes away. Southlake & Westlake carry some of the highest household incomes in the DFW metro.

airports.name: Fort Worth Alliance
airports.notes: quieter alternative when Meacham is busy

name: San Antonio
blurb: River Walk nightlife, Tex-Mex everything, and a holiday-lights spectacle that's one of the best in Texas.

airports.name: San Antonio Intl
airports.notes: right at the edge of comfortable range

name: Houston
blurb: Museum District density, a huge international food scene, and the Texas Renaissance Festival just outside town. River Oaks is the single most prestigious residential neighborhood in Texas — old oil money, the River Oaks Country Club.

airports.name: David Wayne Hooks Memorial
airports.notes: fuel available 24/7, no FBO service agreement complications

name: Albuquerque
blurb: Old Town culture and Sandia views, home to the single most photogenic event in this whole list every October.

airports.name: Albuquerque Intl Sunport / Kirtland AFB
airports.notes: right at the edge of comfortable range

name: Tulsa
blurb: Art Deco district, Philbrook Museum, and one of the largest Oktoberfests in the country — plus a Christmas lights display that draws half a million people.

name: Minneapolis
blurb: Walker Art Center, lakes, a serious food and brewery scene, and a legit concert calendar.

airports.name: Minneapolis-St Paul Intl
airports.notes: 1 stop via Lincoln, NE (KLNK) required

name: Omaha
blurb: Rising food and arts scene in the Old Market district, with a concert calendar that's been landing your Spotify favorites.

airports.name: Offutt AFB
airports.notes: military field, no civilian FBO

name: Des Moines
blurb: Underrated food-and-brewery town with an easygoing pace — the low-key weekend in the rotation.

name: Colorado Springs
blurb: Garden of the Gods, Pikes Peak, and a quieter mountain-town pace when the crew needs a breather weekend. The Broadmoor has held Forbes Five-Star status longer than any hotel in the world, dating to 1918.

name: Phoenix / Scottsdale
blurb: Desert nightlife, Canal Convergence public art, and a warm-weather escape once everyone else is freezing. The Phoenician, Four Seasons Troon North, and the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess anchor peak-season five-star rates of $1,000+/night.

airports.name: Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl
airports.notes: 1 stop via Roswell, NM required

name: Little Rock
blurb: River Market district nightlife and a solid fall festival calendar — an easy, underrated weekend.

name: Wichita
blurb: Old Town district and a growing arts scene — the closest real "getaway" on the list.

name: Springfield
blurb: Route 66 roots, Bass Pro's flagship store, and the gateway to the Ozarks — a flexible bonus swap for any weekend.

name: Guthrie
blurb: Victorian-era downtown, the closest boutique option on the whole list.

name: Waco
blurb: Magnolia Market energy plus a serious rodeo pedigree.

name: Bentonville
blurb: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art anchors a genuinely great little art town.

name: Eureka Springs
blurb: Victorian mountain town, winding streets, a legitimately weird and wonderful Ozarks arts scene.

name: Hot Springs
blurb: Historic bathhouse row plus the longest-running documentary film festival in North America.

name: Fredericksburg
blurb: Texas Hill Country wine town, one of the closest genuine boutique escapes on the list.

name: Taos
blurb: 400 years of art colony history in the shadow of the Sangre de Cristos.

name: Manitou Springs
blurb: Artsy little town at the base of Pikes Peak with a genuinely bizarre Halloween tradition.

name: Bandera
blurb: "Cowboy Capital of the World" — dude ranches, gunfighter shows, and small-town Texas charm.

name: Salida
blurb: Riverside mountain arts town in the Collegiate Peaks.

name: Estes Park
blurb: Gateway to Rocky Mountain National Park, best visited during elk mating season.

name: Marfa
blurb: High-desert art town, minimalist installations, genuinely nowhere else like it.

name: Durango
blurb: Historic narrow-gauge railroad town with real Western-heritage cred.

airports.name: Grand Junction Regional
airports.notes: 1 stop via Pueblo required

name: Terlingua
blurb: Far West Texas ghost town that comes alive once a year for one very specific reason.

name: Sedona
blurb: Red rocks, galleries, and one of the most scenic arts festivals anywhere.

airports.name: Prescott Regional / Ernest Love Field
airports.notes: 1 stop via Santa Fe required

name: Roswell
blurb: UFO Museum, campy alien-themed Americana. Straightforward direct leg, no fuel stop needed.

name: Amarillo
blurb: Cadillac Ranch, Palo Duro Canyon (the "Grand Canyon of Texas"), and the 72oz steak challenge at the Big Texan. Closest real getaway on this list.

name: Lubbock
blurb: Buddy Holly Center, Texas Tech energy, and the Llano Estacado wine region right outside town.

name: Cheyenne
blurb: Curt Gowdy State Park, the Vedauwoo rock formations, and the Frontier Days grounds when the crowds aren't there.

airports.name: Cheyenne Regional
airports.notes: just over comfortable single-leg range

name: El Paso
blurb: Franklin Mountains State Park, Hueco Tanks climbing, and genuinely great border-town food.

airports.name: El Paso Intl
airports.notes: 1 stop via Midland or Roswell required

name: Rapid City
blurb: Mount Rushmore, Crazy Horse Memorial, and Badlands National Park all within about an hour of the field.

airports.name: Rapid City Regional
airports.notes: 1 stop via Colorado Springs or Centennial required

name: Grand Junction
blurb: Palisade wine country, Colorado National Monument, and the Riverfront Trail along the Colorado River.

airports.name: Grand Junction Regional
airports.notes: 1 stop via Pueblo or Colorado Springs required

name: Tucson
blurb: Saguaro National Park, the Sonoran Desert Museum, and the Titan Missile Museum for a Cold War detour.

airports.name: Tucson Intl / KDMA Davis-Monthan
airports.notes: 1 stop via Roswell required

name: Salt Lake City
blurb: Downtown SLC, the Great Salt Lake, and Park City / Deer Valley about 40 minutes from the airport once ski season opens — St. Regis Deer Valley, Stein Eriksen Lodge, Montage Deer Valley.

airports.name: Salt Lake City Intl
airports.notes: 1 stop via Colorado Springs required

name: Prescott
blurb: Whiskey Row, Watson Lake and the Granite Dells, and the closest approved field to the Grand Canyon (2.5hr drive to the South Rim). Grand Canyon airspace is a Special Flight Rules Area — check current charts and get squadron sign-off before routing near it.

airports.name: Prescott Regional
airports.notes: 1 stop via Santa Fe required

name: Vail / Beaver Creek
blurb: The headline luxury pick. Four Seasons Vail, Ritz-Carlton Bachelor Gulch, and the family-run Sonnenalp all sit within the resort villages. Mountain typically opens for ski season mid-November; summer alternative is hiking, fly-fishing, and whitewater rafting.

airports.name: Eagle County Regional
airports.notes: 1 stop via Centennial required

name: Oklahoma City (Nichols Hills)
blurb: The closest genuine old-money enclave in the whole footprint. Nichols Hills is Oklahoma's wealthiest zip code — oil-and-cattle fortunes going back a century, the Oklahoma City Golf & Country Club, tree-lined streets.

airports.name: Wiley Post Airport
airports.notes: Approved Vance field, Atlantic Aviation FBO

name: Las Vegas
blurb: The Strip, world-class residencies, and 24-hour everything. Henderson Executive is a quieter GA alternative to the Class B madness of Harry Reid.

name: Los Angeles
blurb: Arenas, amphitheaters, and a food scene that never stops arguing with itself. Van Nuys is one of the busiest GA fields in the country — expect real Class D traffic.

airports.name: Van Nuys
airports.notes: very high GA traffic, expect sequencing delays

name: San Diego
blurb: Perfect weather, a genuinely great craft beer scene, and Balboa Park's museum row. Montgomery Field keeps you clear of Lindbergh's Class C.

name: San Francisco
blurb: Fog, hills, and one of the country's best gallery and food scenes packed into 7 square miles. Hayward Executive is the practical GA field for the East Bay side.

name: Seattle
blurb: Grunge history, a serious coffee and food culture, and mountains and water in every direction. Boeing Field is the workhorse GA/cargo field just south of downtown.

name: Portland
blurb: Food carts, breweries, and a genuinely weird streak that's part of the brand. Hillsboro is the quieter reliever field west of downtown.

name: Boise
blurb: A small, walkable downtown with the Boise River greenbelt and the Sawtooths within reach. Boise Air Terminal shares a field with Gowen Field ANGB.

airports.name: Boise Air Terminal / Gowen Field
airports.notes: shared with Air National Guard ops

name: Bozeman
blurb: Gateway to Yellowstone and the Bridger range, with a downtown that's outgrown its ranch-town roots. Bozeman Yellowstone Intl handles GA fine outside peak ski-season traffic.

name: Spokane
blurb: Riverfront Park, a compact downtown, and easy access to the Palouse and North Idaho lakes. Felts Field is the historic GA field east of downtown.

name: Jackson
blurb: Grand Teton at your back door and a town square that still means it about the antler arches. The airport sits inside Grand Teton National Park — genuinely rare.

airports.name: Jackson Hole
airports.notes: field is inside Grand Teton NP; noise-sensitive procedures

name: Chicago
blurb: Deep-dish arguments aside, one of the best live-music and museum cities in the country. Chicago Executive avoids O'Hare's Class B entirely.

name: Milwaukee
blurb: Lakefront festivals, a serious beer-and-supper-club culture, and a lot less traffic than Chicago. Timmerman is the close-in GA field on the northwest side.

name: Detroit
blurb: Motown history, a genuine comeback downtown, and a music scene with real depth. Oakland County Intl is the practical GA field north of the city.

name: Indianapolis
blurb: Speedway history, a walkable downtown canal district, and easy access from the whole Midwest. Eagle Creek is the close-in GA field.

name: Louisville
blurb: Bourbon, the Derby, and a food scene that punches well above its size. Bowman Field is one of the oldest continuously operated airports in the country.

name: Nashville
blurb: Broadway honky-tonks, Music Row, and more live music per block than anywhere in the footprint. John C Tune keeps you off BNA's Class C.

name: Memphis
blurb: Beale Street, Stax and Sun Studio history, and barbecue worth the detour. Millington is a former naval air station now flying civilian GA.

airports.name: Millington Regional Jetport
airports.notes: former NAS Memphis

name: Atlanta
blurb: A genuine music and food capital of the South with a skyline to match. DeKalb-Peachtree is the primary GA reliever, well clear of Hartsfield's Class B.

name: Charlotte
blurb: A fast-growing banking-town skyline with a genuinely good food and brewery scene filling in around it. Concord-Padgett is the go-to GA field northeast of downtown.

name: New Orleans
blurb: Second line brass bands, a food culture unlike anywhere else in the country, and a party that doesn't apologize for itself. Lakefront sits right on the lake, minutes from the French Quarter.

name: Birmingham
blurb: A civil-rights-history downtown with a growing food and brewery scene in the old industrial core.

airports.name: Birmingham-Shuttlesworth Intl
airports.notes: has GA services alongside airline traffic

name: Jacksonville
blurb: Beaches, the St. Johns River, and a low-key Florida downtown without the theme-park crowds.

name: Orlando
blurb: Theme parks aside, a real downtown with a solid concert and food scene of its own. Orlando Executive is close-in and avoids MCO's airline traffic entirely.

name: Miami
blurb: South Beach, Wynwood's street art, and a nightlife scene that runs later than anywhere else in the footprint. Opa-locka is the practical GA field north of downtown.

name: Tampa
blurb: A genuinely underrated food and brewery scene along the Riverwalk, with the beaches of St. Pete just across the bay.

name: Charleston
blurb: Cobblestone streets, some of the best food in the South, and a genuinely elegant historic downtown. Executive Field is a quiet GA option south of the city.

name: Savannah
blurb: Spanish moss, squares, and a walkable historic district with a food scene to match Charleston's.

airports.name: Savannah/Hilton Head Intl
airports.notes: has GA services alongside airline traffic

name: New York
blurb: Everything, all the time — Broadway, arenas, and a museum and food scene with no real rival. Teterboro is the classic GA field for Manhattan, but expect real jet traffic and slot coordination.

airports.name: Teterboro
airports.notes: high-traffic corporate jet field; slot/PPR-adjacent coordination common

name: Boston
blurb: Historic, walkable, and packed with music venues and museums. Hanscom Field is the well-known GA alternative to Logan's Class B.

name: Philadelphia
blurb: Deep American history downtown with a food and music scene that's come into its own. Northeast Philadelphia is the practical GA field.

name: Washington
blurb: The Smithsonian alone is worth the trip, with a food and live-music scene that's grown well past the monuments. Airspace here is genuinely restrictive — expect SFRA/FRZ procedures.

airports.name: Montgomery County Airpark
airports.notes: inside the DC SFRA — TSA/FRZ procedures apply

name: Pittsburgh
blurb: Three rivers, a genuinely revitalized downtown, and a food scene built on steel-town bones.

name: Baltimore
blurb: Row-house neighborhoods, a working harbor, and a crab-and-seafood scene worth the trip.

name: Asheville
blurb: Blue Ridge mountain town with more breweries per capita than almost anywhere in the country, plus a genuinely serious art scene.

name: Key West
blurb: End-of-the-road island energy, sunset celebrations on Mallory Square, and Duval Street nightlife. The airport is walkable to Old Town.

name: Napa
blurb: Wine country food and scenery without needing to be a wine person about it. Napa County Airport is a quiet GA field right in the valley.

name: Gatlinburg
blurb: Smoky Mountains gateway with a genuinely touristy but fun strip and some of the best hiking in the East.

name: Door County
blurb: Cherry orchards, fish boils, and a quiet Lake Michigan peninsula that feels a world away from Milwaukee.

name: Traverse City
blurb: Cherry festivals, Lake Michigan beaches, and a genuinely good little food and wine scene up north.

name: Newport
blurb: Gilded Age mansions, the Cliff Walk, and a sailing-town harbor scene.

name: Pensacola
blurb: Naval aviation's home town — the Blue Angels fly out of NAS Pensacola — plus genuinely great white-sand beaches on the Gulf.

airports.name: Pensacola Intl
airports.notes: has GA services alongside airline traffic

name: Shreveport
blurb: Barksdale AFB's home town, with a Red River downtown and a genuine live-music and casino scene.

name: Columbus
blurb: A genuinely good college-town food and brewery scene layered onto a real state-capital downtown.

name: Virginia Beach
blurb: NAS Oceana's home town — an active Navy jet base right behind the boardwalk — plus miles of Atlantic beach.

airports.name: Chesapeake Regional
airports.notes: Oceana itself is military-only; this is the nearest civil GA field

name: Fresno
blurb: Central Valley hub close to Naval Air Station Lemoore, with Yosemite and Sequoia both a reasonable drive away.

name: Sacramento
blurb: California's capital, close to Beale AFB, with a downtown farm-to-fork food scene and easy reach into the Sierra foothills.

airports.name: Sacramento McClellan
airports.notes: former McClellan AFB, now civil

name: Dover
blurb: Dover AFB's home town — a small state-capital downtown on the Delaware Bay side of the peninsula.

name: Trenton
blurb: Close to Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, with a compact state-capital downtown along the Delaware River.

name: Fayetteville
blurb: Fort Liberty's home town — one of the largest military installations in the world (XVIII Airborne Corps, Special Forces).

name: Columbus
blurb: Fort Moore's home town — Army infantry and Airborne/Ranger training — with a genuinely fun whitewater rafting run right through downtown.

name: Killeen
blurb: Fort Cavazos's home town — one of the largest Army posts in the country by population.

airports.name: Killeen-Fort Cavazos Regional
airports.notes: joint-use with Fort Cavazos

name: Clarksville
blurb: Fort Campbell's home town — the 101st Airborne — with an easy drive into Nashville when you want more going on.

name: Lawton
blurb: Fort Sill's home town — Army Field Artillery — and the closest thing to a fellow OK military town from Vance.

airports.name: Lawton-Fort Sill Regional
airports.notes: joint-use with Fort Sill

name: Junction City
blurb: Fort Riley's home town, with Manhattan (KSU) close enough for a real college-town night out.

name: Watertown
blurb: Fort Drum's home town — the 10th Mountain Division — a long way from any of the departure bases but genuinely close to the Thousand Islands and the Adirondacks.

name: Columbia
blurb: Fort Jackson's home town — the Army's largest basic training post — with a real state-capital downtown to go with it.

name: Augusta
blurb: Fort Eisenhower's home town (Army Cyber Command) — and, one week a year, the Masters.

name: Radcliff
blurb: Fort Knox's home town — yes, that Fort Knox — with Louisville a reasonable drive north for a real night out.

name: Huntsville
blurb: Redstone Arsenal's home town — Army missile defense and NASA's rocket-development heart — with a genuinely good and fast-growing food and brewery scene to match.

airports.name: Huntsville Executive / Tom Sharp Jr Field

name: Leesville
blurb: Fort Johnson's home town — home of the Army's Joint Readiness Training Center — genuinely remote, closest real airport is in Alexandria.

airports.name: England Airpark
airports.notes: former England AFB, now civil

name: Tacoma
blurb: Joint Base Lewis-McChord's home town — Army and Air Force sharing one of the busiest bases in the country — with Mt. Rainier at your back door and Seattle a short hop north.

name: Altus
blurb: Another Oklahoma Air Force town — Altus flies the C-17 and KC-46 schoolhouse — small, quiet, and about as no-frills as this list gets.

airports.name: Altus AFB
airports.notes: active-duty field, PPR required for transients

name: Wichita Falls
blurb: Sheppard AFB's home town — undergraduate pilot training for the Air Force and NATO's Euro-NATO Joint Jet Pilot Training program both fly out of here.

airports.name: Sheppard AFB / Wichita Falls Municipal
airports.notes: joint-use: Sheppard AFB shares the field with the civilian terminal

name: Abilene
blurb: Dyess AFB's home town — B-1 bombers, and soon B-21s — with a real West Texas downtown around it.

name: San Angelo
blurb: Goodfellow AFB's home town — intelligence and fire-protection training — with a genuinely nice riverwalk downtown.

name: Biloxi
blurb: Keesler AFB's home town — Air Force technical training on the Mississippi Gulf Coast, casinos and beaches included.

name: Panama City
blurb: Tyndall AFB's home town — F-22s over some of the whitest sand beaches on the Gulf.

name: Valdosta
blurb: Moody AFB's home town — A-10s and combat rescue — a straightforward South Georgia stop.

name: Warner Robins
blurb: Robins AFB's home town — Air Force Materiel Command's depot maintenance hub — with Macon close enough for real food and music.

name: Montgomery
blurb: Maxwell AFB's home town — Air University, where every Air Force officer eventually passes through — layered onto genuinely important civil rights history downtown.

name: Minot
blurb: Minot AFB's home town — B-52s and Minuteman III missile fields — about as far north as this list reaches.

name: Great Falls
blurb: Malmstrom AFB's home town — another Minuteman III missile wing — right on the Missouri River with genuinely good fishing and hiking around it.

airports.name: Great Falls Intl
airports.notes: shared civil/military field with Malmstrom

name: Knob Noster
blurb: Whiteman AFB's home town — the B-2 stealth bomber's only base — small and quiet, closest real airport is in Warrensburg.

name: Norfolk
blurb: Naval Station Norfolk is the largest naval base in the world — a real downtown and a genuinely good Navy history museum built around it.

name: Hampton
blurb: Joint Base Langley-Eustis's home town — F-22s at Langley, Army logistics at Eustis — right on the Chesapeake.

name: Jacksonville
blurb: Camp Lejeune's home town — one of the Marine Corps' largest bases — with the New River and the Crystal Coast close by.

name: Oceanside
blurb: Camp Pendleton's home town — a real Marine Corps base with a genuinely good beach town built around it, San Diego a short hop south.

name: Buffalo
blurb: Buffalo wings at the source, Niagara Falls 25 minutes north, and a genuinely revitalized Canalside waterfront. Bills home games are the draw.

name: Cincinnati
blurb: Over-the-Rhine's historic district anchors a real food and brewery scene, plus Cincinnati chili if you're brave. Bengals home games are the draw.

name: Cleveland
blurb: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Playhouse Square's theater district, and a lakefront downtown with a real food scene at West Side Market. Browns home games are the draw.

name: Green Bay
blurb: Lambeau Field and the Titletown District are basically the whole draw — small downtown, Bay Beach amusement park on the water for the day before kickoff.

name: Fort Smith
blurb: Old frontier town on the Arkansas River — the U.S. Marshals Museum, Garrison Avenue, and a downtown covered in murals from The Unexpected festival. Ebbing ANGB shares the field and hosts the foreign F-35 pilot training center.

airports.name: Fort Smith Regional
airports.notes: joint-use: Ebbing ANGB shares the field with the civilian terminal

name: Norman
blurb: OU's home — SEC football at Owen Field is the headline, with Campus Corner and Main Street around it. Westheimer is the university's own airport, a few minutes from campus.

name: Stillwater
blurb: Oklahoma State and the birthplace of Red Dirt music — Eskimo Joe's, the Strip, and Cowboys football at Boone Pickens Stadium. Barely a hop from Vance.

name: Branson
blurb: The live-show capital of the Ozarks — the 76 Strip, Silver Dollar City, and Table Rock Lake. Branson Airport has the long runway; the downtown field is closer but short.

airports.name: Branson Airport
airports.notes: downtown KPLK is closer but only 3,738 ft

name: Hochatown / Broken Bow
blurb: Cabin country in the Kiamichi foothills — Beavers Bend State Park, Broken Bow Lake and the Mountain Fork River, with breweries and a distillery in Hochatown itself.

airports.name: McCurtain County Regional
airports.notes: 5,002 ft; Broken Bow Muni (90F) is closer but only 3,200 ft
